LESSON: PRONUNCIATION AND LISTENING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.1.1: Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why should you pronounce words correctly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify proverbs from a text for effective communication
2. listen for the main idea and specific details from a text
3. use words and expressions such as similes, metaphors and proverbs containing selected sounds correctly

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension

Teach
• Focus skill: identify proverbs from a text for effective communication.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should you pronounce words correctly?
2. Why do we use proverbs?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
